Get or Set State Names

Source: R/05_tools.R
state_names.Rd

Utilities for assigning and retrieving the state names associated with stochastic vectors, stochastic matrices, and Markov chains.

set_state_names() assigns default sequential state names when names are missing. Existing names are preserved.

get_state_names() retrieves the state names attached to an object.

Usage

set_state_names(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'StochVec'
set_state_names(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'StochMat'
set_state_names(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
set_state_names(x, ...)

get_state_names(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'StochVec'
get_state_names(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'StochMat'
get_state_names(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'MarkovChain'
get_state_names(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
get_state_names(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A StochVec, StochMat, or, for get_state_names(), a MarkovChain object.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods. Currently unused.

Value

set_state_names() returns x with state names assigned where necessary.

get_state_names() returns a character vector containing the state names.

Details

For an unnamed StochVec, set_state_names() assigns the names "1", "2", ..., according to the vector length.

For a StochMat, missing row or column names are assigned as "1", "2", ..., according to the matrix dimensions. After assignment, the row and column names must be identical. An error is raised when they differ.

State names must be unique, non-missing, and non-empty.

For a MarkovChain, get_state_names() retrieves the row names of its transition matrix.

Examples

a <- StochVec(c(0.4, 0.6))
get_state_names(a)
#> [1] "1" "2"

P <- StochMat(matrix(c(0.8, 0.2,
                       0.3, 0.7),
                     nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))
get_state_names(P)
#> [1] "1" "2"

named_a <- StochVec(c(low = 0.4, high = 0.6))
get_state_names(named_a)
#> [1] "low"  "high"

named_P <- StochMat(
  matrix(c(0.8, 0.2,
           0.3, 0.7),
         nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE,
         dimnames = list(c("low", "high"), c("low", "high")))
)
get_state_names(named_P)
#> [1] "low"  "high"

mc <- MarkovChain(a = named_a, P = named_P)
get_state_names(mc)
#> [1] "low"  "high"
